supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:56 UTC, mia.santos ran PowerShell from Explorer to compress \\FILE-BLU-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\mia.santos\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; the process ran at medium integrity.
Sysmon recorded creation of c.zip at 13:45:00 UTC, shortly after the archive command.

At 13:50:36 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01 connected through the proxy to bigsend-drop.net with 51,000,000 client-to-server tunnel bytes; Zeek recorded 51,000,299 originating bytes and only 9,029 response bytes. The associated proxy connection was made by Chrome running as mia.santos.

The close sequence and scale—creating an archive of the Clients share, then sending about 51 MB to a destination not among the approved services—strongly indicates likely data exfiltration. The records do not directly link c.zip to the proxy transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy record identifies the destination and byte counts, but does not expose the upload URL, payload contents, or uploaded filename (T209-00202).
The network records associate the transfer with Chrome and mia.santos, but do not establish which local file Chrome sent (T209-00204, T209-00205).
claims_not_established: The evidence does not prove that c.zip was the file transferred or establish the archive's exact contents or size.
The evidence does not establish whether mia.santos had a business reason or authorization for the archive or transfer.
The records do not identify the recipient account, ultimate recipient, or what happened to the data after transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect c.zip and endpoint file-system or EDR telemetry to establish its size, contents, hash, and whether it was read by Chrome.
Obtain detailed proxy, TLS inspection, or DLP records for the bigsend-drop.net session, including request metadata and any available upload filename or account.
Confirm with mia.santos and the relevant data owner whether the archive and external transfer were authorized.
unrelated_findings: At 13:49:53 UTC, DC-BLU-01 recorded Kerberos ticket activity for ruth.moss originating from WS-MSANTOS-01's IP, followed by a network logon as ruth.moss to WS-RMOSS-01 from that same IP. This is outside the alerted transfer and should be reviewed separately; the records alone do not establish why it occurred. (T209-00197, T209-00199, T209-00201)
